To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
a novel double-flowered torena mutant was obtained from the progeny of the Ttf1 transposon-active “Flecked mutant”.

a double-flower trait was obtained in torenia by insertion of T. fournieri Ttf1 into TfFAR, a C-class floral homeobox gene, whereas the transposon was excised from TfFAR, resulting in reversion of petals to staminate structures.

a novel “petaloid” mutant of torenia, in which 4 stamens are converted to 4 petals, was obtained from self-pollen of the “flecked” mutant and that the double-flower trait is unstable, but can be stabilized by genetic separation between the transposon and its activator.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the molecular mechanism of floral homeosis in Torenia.
the development of a double-flowered torena mutant by insertion of TTF1 into a floral homeotic gene.
the development of a novel “Petaloid“ double-flower mutant of torenia, which is useful for the breeding of ornamental plants.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the “Petaloids” phenotype is caused by the insertion of Ttf2 into TfFAR.
the “Petaloids” mutant is a C-class floral homeosis mutant caused by insertion of the DNA transposable element Ttf1 into TfFAR.
the insertion of Ttf 1 into the C-class floral gene TfFAR causes the double-flower phenotype in the “Petalold” mutant.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

a “Petaloid-like” double flower can be obtained by inactivating the C-class floral organ identity gene in a single flower, whereas the “Petal” mutation can be obtained by activating the transposon in the entire genome.
a “Petaloid-like” mutant of torenia could be generated through a single transposition event of Ttf1, whereas its double-flower phenotype was unstable because of the transposon excision.

we obtained a novel “Petaloid“ mutant of Torenia through the insertion of Ttf 1 into the TfFAR gene, and that the double-flower trait is unstable because of the excision of the Ttf1 element from the TfFAR locus.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the DNA transposons are powerful molecular tools for genetic modification of plants.
the double-flower trait is controlled by homozygous alleles of the C-class homeotic gene TfFAR with a transposon insertion.
the “Petalold” mutation is caused by the insertion of the Ttf1 transposon into the 2 ^{nd} intron of Tf FAR and the resulting inhibition of expression of the C- class floral homeotic gene, Tf FAR.
